short: Prime minister at twenty-four; he organised Britain against revolutionary France.
full:
William Pitt the Younger became prime minister in December 1783 at the age of twenty-four, the youngest ever, and was widely expected to last weeks. He won a crushing majority in the 1784 election and stayed seventeen years. He rebuilt public finances after the loss of America, cutting duties to undercut smuggling, establishing a sinking fund to retire debt, and in 1799 levying Britain's first income tax to pay for war.

The French Revolution redefined him. He suspended habeas corpus, prosecuted radicals and assembled successive coalitions against France, financing allies with British subsidies. His Act of Union of 1800 abolished the Irish parliament; when George III refused the Catholic emancipation Pitt regarded as its necessary companion, he resigned in March 1801. He returned in 1804, saw Nelson win at Trafalgar and Napoleon win at Austerlitz within seven weeks of each other, and died in office in January 1806, aged forty-six and heavily in debt.
